title: The G-ring property passes from an affine open cover to every affine open
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ be an affine open covering. If every ring $\mathcal O_X(U_i)$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], then for every affine open $V\subseteq X$ the ring $\mathcal O_X(V)$ is a G-ring.

proof.text: Write $A_i=\mathcal O_X(U_i)$. Each $A_i$ is Noetherian by the G-ring definition [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. The given affine cover therefore witnesses that $X$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth].

Fix an arbitrary affine open $V\subseteq X$ and put $B=\mathcal O_X(V)$. Since $X$ is locally Noetherian, [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth] gives that $B$ is Noetherian. It remains, by [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], to check the completion map at each prime of $B$.

source.place: Tag 01OW (lemma-locally-Noetherian), as used in Tags 0HA4 and 0HA5.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q$ be any prime of $B$. The canonical open immersion of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points] sends $\mathfrak q$ to a point $x\in V$. Choose $i$ with $x\in U_i$ and let $\mathfrak p$ be its corresponding prime of $A_i$. By clause (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] for $V$ and for $U_i$, there are ring isomorphisms $B_{\mathfrak q}\cong\mathcal O_{X,x}\cong(A_i)_{\mathfrak p}$. Composing them gives $e:(A_i)_{\mathfrak p}\xrightarrow{\sim}B_{\mathfrak q}$.

source.place: Tag 0HA4, implication (1) implies (2), and the affine-local interpretation in its final paragraph; Schemes Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), via affine-open stalk localizations.

proof.text: Put $R=(A_i)_{\mathfrak p}$ and $S=B_{\mathfrak q}$, with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_R$ and $\mathfrak m_S$. The equivalence $e:R\cong S$ carries nonunits to nonunits (an inverse to $e(r)$ pulls back to an inverse to $r$), so $e(\mathfrak m_R)=\mathfrak m_S$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-ring-equiv] to these ideals. It supplies $E:\widehat R\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat S$ such that $E\circ\iota_R=\iota_S\circ e$, where $\iota_R$ and $\iota_S$ are the canonical maximal-ideal completion maps.

source.place: Tag 0HA4, stalk identifications with localizations; completion transport from algebra.tex Section 00M9 and More on Algebra Definition 07GH.

proof.text: The map $\iota_R:R\to\widehat R$ is regular because $A_i$ is a G-ring and $\mathfrak p$ is a prime of $A_i$, by [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-map-ring-equiv] to $f=\iota_R$, $g=\iota_S$, $a=e$, $b=E$, and the equality from step 4. Its conclusion is that $\iota_S:B_{\mathfrak q}\to\widehat{B_{\mathfrak q}}$ is regular.

source.place: Tag 0HA4, regular local completion maps; More on Algebra Tags 07GH (definition-G-ring) and 07BZ (definition-regular).

proof.text: The ring $B$ is Noetherian by step 2 and its completion maps at every prime $\mathfrak q$ are regular by steps 3–5. These are exactly the defining conditions of a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Thus $\mathcal O_X(V)$ is a G-ring for every affine open $V$.
